first_impression.reaction: Intro is three short paragraphs and the Key takeaways are right under it, so I'm not scrolling through fluff. But I typed 'brazilian wedding traditions' and the takeaways only give me three customs, then a line about notarial appointments in Brasília. I wanted a quick list of the traditions. I'd keep going because the headings look scannable.

journey.quote: This guide walks through Brazilian wedding traditions in the order they tend to happen, from the noivado to the sweets handed out as guests leave.
journey.reaction: Good, tells me what I'm getting and in what order. Quick to read on my phone.

journey.quote: Australians marrying in Brazil should confirm documents with the cartório first, then book any notarial appointment in Brasília or São Paulo, not Rio de Janeiro.
journey.reaction: I'm not Australian and I didn't ask about paperwork. One of four takeaways is spent on this, while the dress hem, the groom's tie and Santo Antônio aren't in there at all. Feels like the summary is for someone else.

journey.quote: Bem-casados, small sponge cakes made of two halves, are the sweet many couples hand to guests as they leave.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of thing I came for. Specific and quick.

journey.section: Noivado and the ring on the right hand
journey.quote: Many couples wear their alianças on the right hand while engaged and move them to the left hand during the wedding.
journey.reaction: Nice, that's a fact I didn't know and can repeat to friends. It answers the title.

journey.section: Noivado and the ring on the right hand
journey.quote: In Portuguese, noivado means the relationship between two people who are going to marry, the time it lasts, and the occasion when the commitment is made official, generally with a party.
journey.reaction: Bit dictionary-ish. I'd skim past it. Same with the Priberam and Michaelis lines further down; I believe you, I just don't need the citation in the sentence.

journey.quote: It is often told that whoever's name has worn away by the end of the night will be the next to marry.
journey.reaction: This is the fun 'you did not know' stuff. Short and clear. I like that it says 'often told' instead of pretending it's a rule.

journey.quote: Neither is a wedding custom in UNESCO's description.
journey.reaction: Honest, but then why are three paragraphs about them under a wedding traditions heading? I'd have skipped this section if the heading said so.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Brazil as an Australian
journey.quote: This section reflects official sources as at November 2026.
journey.reaction: Dated, which I like. But the whole legal and Smartraveller block is long and not my question. I'd scroll straight past it to the FAQ.

journey.quote: Many Brazilian couples wear the aliança on the right ring finger during the engagement and move it to the left ring finger at the wedding.
journey.reaction: Direct answer, first line. This FAQ is useful and probably what I'd screenshot.
Just tell me roughly how much it costs. I get why there's no number, but it's a bit of a non-answer.

unanswered_questions: Is there a quick list of all the traditions in one place? I had to piece it together from the headings.
What do the couple and guests typically wear, or is there a traditional colour?
Are there any traditions at the actual church ceremony itself, like the entrance or vows?

turn_offs_found.quote: Australians marrying in Brazil should confirm documents with the cartório first, then book any notarial appointment in Brasília or São Paulo, not Rio de Janeiro.
turn_offs_found.why: Takes a Key takeaways slot from the actual traditions I searched for, and assumes I'm Australian.

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Brazilian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly clickbaity title, and the headings don't then flag which ones are the surprising ones.

would_share_with: A friend going to a Brazilian wedding, mainly for the bem-casados, ring and names-in-the-hem bits

cta_reaction.quote: If that sounds useful, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: I'm not planning a wedding, I just wanted the traditions. The pitch is low-key and not annoying, so it doesn't put me off the page, but I won't click.

top_3_changes: Make the Key takeaways (or a short list right after the intro) name the traditions themselves: rings right to left hand, padrinhos, chá de panela, names in the hem, groom's tie, bem-casados. Move the cartório line lower or out of the takeaways.
Trim the dictionary attributions inside the custom sections (Michaelis, Priberam) so each custom reads as one quick line on what happens and what it means.
Retitle or relabel the Music and dance section so it's clear it's regional music, not a wedding custom, or cut it down to a sentence.

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional (search-intent proxy, weight 0.10). Should the Key takeaways rebalance toward customs be weighed against the Australian-couple personas who may value the legal takeaway?

assumptions: Read on a phone; skimmed intro, Key takeaways, custom sections and FAQ; skimmed past the legal and travel sections as this persona would.
Missing cost figure treated as low severity per the orchestrator: no prices is the standard.
